findings.title: The public `findMany` API was removed without an equivalent query API
findings.body: This change deletes `InsightsBookingService.findMany`, which previously accepted normal Prisma findMany arguments and applied the authorization and filter conditions before reading `BookingTimeStatusDenormalized`. The replacement only returns a SQL fragment, so existing callers of this exported service will either fail TypeScript compilation or fail at runtime, and callers must now reimplement selection, pagination, ordering, and any additional where clauses themselves. Preserve a compatible query method or migrate every production consumer as part of the change.

findings.title: Constructor type accepts an invalid team scope as valid input
findings.body: `InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions` permits `{ scope: "team", userId, orgId }` because `teamId` is optional for every scope. The constructor accepts that value at this line, but `safeParse` rejects it against the discriminated schema and the service silently returns `1=0`. Before this change, the constructor required `InsightsBookingServiceOptions`, which required `teamId` for team scope at compile time. Make the public type a discriminated union with a required `teamId` in the team variant, or accept `unknown` explicitly if invalid external input is intentionally supported.

findings.title: No database test executes the new team or org SQL conditions
findings.body: The only test that interpolates the generated condition into `$queryRaw` uses `scope: "user"`, which only exercises scalar `userId`/`teamId IS NULL` predicates. Team and org scopes now generate `ANY(${number[]})` raw parameters and OR-combined authorization predicates, but their tests only compare `Prisma.Sql` objects; those comparisons recreate the same template and do not validate PostgreSQL syntax, array parameter serialization, or the rows actually authorized. Add `$queryRaw` integration coverage for both scopes with included and excluded bookings.
